s001.text: UPSC, twenty seventeen. General Studies Paper One, fifteen marks, two hundred and fifty words. What characteristics can be assigned to the monsoon climate? It feeds more than fifty per cent of the world's people in Monsoon Asia. Here's the catch. About half of humanity is easy to prove. More than half is not.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Can be assigned means list the traits of the climate. That feeds means link it to food. So there are three jobs. The traits. The link to food. And a check on the premise.

s003.text: Start with the traits. Monsoon means a seasonal reversal of winds. South and South-East Asia have it from June to September. East Asia has its own, from June to August. Japan's Baiu runs from early June to late July.

s004.text: But the rain is not even. India gets nearly seventy-five per cent of its yearly rain in four months. It starts in Kerala about the first of June. And it swings about ten per cent from year to year, with dry breaks.

s005.text: Now the link to food. It is rice. Asia grows eighty-nine per cent of the world's rice. FAO says rice is central to the food security of about half of humanity. And rice needs over one hundred centimetres of rain, or irrigation.

s006.text: But check the premise. Add East, South-East and South Asia, and you get fifty-four per cent of the world. That counts whole regions, so it is an upper bound. And it was already fifty-two per cent in nineteen fifty. So write: about half.

s007.text: Now we write. Two hundred and fifty words, about eleven minutes. Open with the definition. Then give the safe figure: about half of humanity.

s008.text: Section one is the traits. Wind reversal. Two systems with their months. Rain packed into four months. And a swing of about ten per cent, with El Niño as one cause.

s009.text: Section two is the feeding. Rice is the bridge. Asia's share, FAO's wording, and five big producers, all in the belt. Add one diagram: four bars, drawn in a minute. People, rice, top five, and rain alone.

s010.text: Section three tests the premise. Fifty-four per cent is an upper bound. About forty per cent of Asia's rice depends on rain alone. FAO names rainfall instability a main risk. Close on that. The variability, not the size, is the risk.

s011.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It says over half, exactly, with no figure behind it. It says the monsoon is regular. It says rice grows only in India and China. It treats monsoon as Indian summer rain alone. And it names no number or source. Both took eleven minutes. Only one tested the premise.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. The same frame answers its cousins. Twenty eighteen asked for the origin, progress and retreat of the monsoon. Twenty twenty-two asked why it is unpredictable. Learn it once: the traits, the link, the check.
